lines.text: each man has his own individual life to live and his own
individual death to die in sole responsibility before God.
When man forgets this he violates his own dignity just as
much as he violates the dignity of nature in equating his own
structures with the powers and manifestations of nature. But
if he violates the dignity of his humanity he also violates the
honour of God who created man in His own image. And then
he falls under the shadow of annihilating judgment. For
if he forgets that he has to live his life in responsibility before
God, his life becomes a dark mystery to him and his death a
terror. He cannot of course truly understand his life in terms
of the natural growth and development of plants and
animals, for his life is always intertwined with responsibility
and decision, temptation and guilt. Neither can he under-
stand his death in terms of the withering and decay of
vegetable life, as something utterly natural and self-
explanatory. Rather to grow old and die is something that is
repugnant and incomprehensible to him; it is fraught with
terror. And though at all times loud voices have been raised
in the endeavour to soothe and delude man's troubled spirit
as it recoils in horror from his mysterious destiny, anguish
breaks out in him ever afresh. For the man who knows God
only in the realm of nature, death implies destruction, a
destruction which makes his whole life meaningless.
Finally, a last word. If man goes no further than to be
stirred by nature to feelings of devout gratitude, if he is not
driven onwards to seek the face of the Creator, then his piety,
however genuine, remains merely episodic and fragmentary.
It remains as something which from time to time is
awakened to life, which gives a religious tone to certain
hours, which may indeed become vividly felt in the spring
but which fades away again with the withering of the flowers.
For the God whose presence man experiences in the bright-
ness of nature, ceases to be felt in the grey light of common
day, in the pressures of responsibility, in the storms of fate.
